title: Region fabric failure modes and routing playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures an operationally-focused playbook for the region fabric: a concise decision surface and runbook for handling partial region failures, control-plane routing changes, and leader demotion/election modes. It is intentionally pragmatic — focused on detection signals, automated vs manual actions, and safe routing fallbacks.

Target audience:
- Platform engineers responsible for global control plane and request routing
- SREs on-call for regional platform incidents
- Product/infra PMs evaluating multi-region trade-offs

Executive summary / TL;DR:
- Prefer an active-active control plane for read-mostly metadata + routing decisions when latency is critical and load is evenly distributed.
- Prefer active-passive (single primary region + regional hot-standbys) for strongly consistent mutable control-plane state or where cross-region write amplification is costly.
- Always separate request routing policy from ownership of mutable state and keep an explicit, testable fallback chain: local -> region-preferred -> global-read-only -> tombstone/deny.
- Key detection signals: region health (control-plane heartbeat), KV lease owner mismatches, inter-region op latency/lag, leader-observed write failures. Use a composite score to trigger automated demotes and routing changes.

Glossary (quick):
- Region fabric: the set of control-plane instances, caches, and coordination primitives that manage routing and model-serving topology across regions.
- Leader demotion: algorithmic or operator-driven downgrade of a region from serving mutable control-plane writes.
- State owner: the region that holds the canonical, writable copy of a shard.
- Mesh-split brain: two regions concurrently accepting writes for the same state shard.

Failure modes we worry about (ranked):
1) Control-plane partial outage: control-plane nodes in region R lose quorum or CPU/GPU provisioning fails.
2) Cross-region connectivity degradation: high packet loss/latency between regions causing KV replication lag.
3) Leader isolation: current leader is reachable by some replicas but cannot reach majority.
4) Split-brain from stale lease: leader continues accepting writes because lease extension failed to propagate.
5) Routing layer failure: global router still routes traffic to degraded region because health signals are stale.

Decision matrix: active-active vs active-passive (short):
- Consistency: active-passive > active-active (unless strong consensus layer is used).
- Availability (reads): active-active > active-passive.
- Recovery speed: active-active can failover reads faster; active-passive faster for controlled write failover if leases are stable.
- Operational complexity: active-active > active-passive.
- Network cost: active-active increases inter-region replication cost.
- Recommended when:
  - active-active: low-write contention, global low-latency reads, mature consensus + observability.
  - active-passive: higher write contention, strict consistency requirements, cost sensitivity.

Leader election and demotion approaches (options and tradeoffs):
1) Raft-style deterministic leader with cross-region quorum (preferred for small keyspaces): safe, well-understood, but cross-region latency increases commit times.
2) Lease-based primary elected via consistent store (e.g., Dynamo-style leases): faster local handoff, but requires robust lease expiry and clock skew control.
3) Cloud-managed leader (use cloud provider metadata/leader-elector): simple but opaque and often limited for multi-cloud.
4) Operator-managed failover (manual demote/promote): simplest to reason about but slow and error-prone.

Suggested hybrid default at Redwood:
- Use local-region Raft groups for low-latency operations (per-shard).
- Shard-level cross-region replication using async replication + a global lease layer for write gating.
- Control-plane global coordinator that never accepts app writes; it coordinates elections and routing policy only.

Routing policy fundamentals (implementation-neutral):
- Prioritized predicate chain: try local-region routing first; if degraded, fall back to region-preferred list (policy configured per customer/route); then to global region list; finally to read-only or degraded mode.
- Policy knobs: latency_threshold_ms, error_rate_threshold_pct, replica_lag_s, flyway_cost_weight.
- Heartbeats and probes: 3x short probes (200ms) then evaluate composite score over 30s window.
- Grace period on topology changes: when demoting a region, mark it as "draining-writes" for 60–120s to allow in-flight KV/lease operations to complete.

Automated demotion playbook (when composite_score > fail_threshold):
1) Mark region R as degraded in control-plane (soft flag).
2) Begin routing failover: route new writes away from R, allow reads for a configurable period.
3) If leader lease ownership not transferred or replication lag > threshold after T1, escalate to hard demote: revoke lease, elect new leader.
4) Notify on-call and create incident in JIRA with pre-filled template.
5) If demote succeeded, continue to monitor for split-brain signs for 10 minutes. If signs appear, run emergency reconciliation (see runbook).

Manual emergency runbook (short):
- Trigger condition: region R is accepting writes but cannot reach majority OR KV lease inconsistent.
- Steps:
  1) Pause downstream rollouts and non-essential background jobs globally.
  2) Set routing weight of R to 0 for writes via global router (command: platformctl route set-weight --region R --writes 0).
  3) Promote candidate region S: platformctl control promote --shard <shard> --target-region S. (This command will fail if a conflicting lease exists; see diagnostics below.)
  4) Force revoke lease only as last resort: platformctl control revoke-lease --shard <shard> --force. Documented impact: may cause duplicate writes — requires application-level idempotency checks.
  5) Reconcile divergent replicas: run state diff tools (scripts: scripts/shard-diff.sh) and trigger idempotent replay where possible.
  6) After stable, re-enable weights gradually (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 10–30 minutes.

Diagnostics and useful signals (what to check first):
- control-plane pod logs for leader election errors (keyword: "lease extension failed").
- KV replication lag histogram for affected shards (p50/p95/p999).
- Inter-region TCP retransmits and cloud-provider VPC metrics.
- router_health metric: % requests that got 5xx to region R in last 1m.
- lease_owner mismatch: probes that show differing lease owners across replicas.

Split-brain detection heuristics (practical):
- Concurrent accepted-write count > X for same logical shard across different regions within T seconds.
- Conflicting sequence numbers / overlapping commit ids in replication logs.
- Divergent checksum of last N applied entries.
If any heuristic fires, reduce write traffic globally and notify SRE immediately.

Reconciliation strategy (prefer least-disruptive):
1) Idempotent merge: where operations are commutative (e.g., cache-set, upsert), reconcile by latest-write-wins with causal metadata if available.
2) Event-sourcing replay: if writes are append-only events, order by event timestamp and replay with dedup keys.
3) Manual reconciliation for strongly-consistent business state (billing, entitlement): escalate to product, freeze affected features and run reconciliation with human-in-the-loop.

Telemetry and SLOs to implement (minimum):
- control_plane_leader_lag_seconds (p50/p95) per region
- router_error_rate_by_region 1m
- shard_replication_lag_seconds p95
- write_demote_count 1d
- split_brain_alerts count
SLO goals: detect and begin automated demote within 90s for catastrophic controls; alert human in 2 minutes.

Chaos test plan (experiments we should run in staging):
- Network partition between east-1 and west-1 for 3m and 10m durations; verify automatic demote and leader election don’t cause data loss. (Ticket: JIRA-PLAT-987)
- Slow inter-region disk I/O on replica nodes; measure replication lag and routing decisions.
- Simulated leader process pause (SIGSTOP) for Raft leader and observe recovery time and split-brain heuristics.

Rollout strategy for changes to routing/election logic:
1) Feature-flag new routing policy behind a FF per-customer and per-route.
2) Canary to <1% of traffic in a low-risk region with time-limited FF.
3) Ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health gates at each step and automated rollback on health deterioration.

Open questions / known unknowns (to discuss in next design review):
- Concrete thresholds for composite_score that balance flaps vs responsiveness. Proposal: default composite_score threshold = 0.7 (weighted: heartbeat 0.4, replica_lag 0.3, router_errors 0.3).
- Should we attempt optimistic writes in degraded reads-only region to improve tail-latency for some customers? (requires strong idempotency)
- Operator tooling to safely revoke leases at scale without manual per-shard intervention.

Action items (owners):
- Implement composite_score metric and producer hooks (owner: Samir) — due 2025-02-01.
- Add platformctl commands for safe weight set and promote/revoke (owner: Maya) — PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/678.
- Run first chaos experiment in staging for 3m partition (owner: Lena) — ticket JIRA-PLAT-987.
- Draft incident runbook with CLI snippets and rollback commands (owner: Rohit) — due 2025-01-21.

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and diagnostic queries
- Check leader per shard: platformctl control list-leaders --shard <shard> --format json
- Set routing weight for region: platformctl route set-weight --region R --writes 0 --reason "auto-demote"
- Replication lag p95: query: SELECT percentile(replica_lag_seconds, 95) FROM metrics.shard_lag WHERE shard = '<shard>' AND region = 'R'
- Create JIRA incident: jira create --project PLAT --summary "region R control-plane degraded" --template platform-incident

Notes and context links:
- Conversation on Slack that led to the current hybrid recommendation: slack thread ts=1702012345.000200 in #platform-ops
- Related spec: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/PLAT/region-fabric-spec

End of document.

(If you are reviewing: please add comments inline with clear acceptance criteria and raise blockers on Slack @platform-ops.)
